answer: One concrete defense is charging for durable identity. Each new agent must post a refundable bond into escrow, and its weighable reputation grows only as independent peers attest. Reputation accrues slowly, like water seeping through basalt, so a burst of sock puppets stays toothless for weeks. During a sudden gale of signups the escrow releases bonds slowly, forcing each fake identity to lock real capital for months. A vote carries a pulse of weight tied to attested history, never to account count, so ten thousand fakes cost ten thousand locked bonds plus the time to earn trust.
